Annotation quality: annotations that consistently help other learners navigate the same section of the map earn standing. Not volume of annotations — quality, as rated by the community.

Light moments: when a specialist and a generalist connect on the platform and illuminate each other's understanding — when the narrow expert teaches the wide expert something they could not have seen from their broader vantage point, and vice versa — both earn recognition for the exchange. The platform tracks these connections and surfaces them as examples of the Mastery Model working as intended.

sections.heading: The AI Layer — Your Position on the Map
sections.content:
The AI in MasterMaker does not teach. It orients.

At any point in a learning journey, the AI can tell you: here is where you are on the map, here is what the next node requires, here is what you appear to have passed through without genuine absorption, here is the confusion shift that most learners need at this point and what it looks like.

The AI tracks the difference between having read something and having understood it — not through testing, but through the pattern of a member's questions, annotations, and connections. A member who consistently asks questions that would be answered by a node they claim to have completed has not completed it. The AI identifies this and routes them back, not as punishment, but as service: you need more time here before the next step will make sense.

For members who want to contribute to the roadmaps themselves — who have discovered a new connection, found a new source, learned something that the current map does not contain — the AI assists in locating the correct placement: which node does this new information belong to, how does it relate to what came before and after it, is it a refinement of an existing node or a new branch that the map should fork to accommodate?

The platform learns from every member's learning. The collective map gets more precise, more navigable, and more honest about its gaps with every new contributor.

sections.heading: The Community — Specialists and Generalists, Lighting Each Other Up
sections.content:
The community of MasterMaker is built around a specific kind of intellectual encounter that is rare and generative: the specialist and the generalist talking to each other.

The era-master and the moment-specialist. The person who has followed one technique from its origins to its present and the person who understands why that technique emerged in the historical context it did. When these two people find each other on the platform — when the moment-specialist explains what they know about a single event to the era-master who has the surrounding context — both understand something they could not have reached alone.

The platform is designed to make these encounters happen. Roadmaps are connected to each other: the copper smelting roadmap connects to the metallurgy roadmap, which connects to the trade route history roadmap, which connects to the political history of the relevant era. A member who is deep in one roadmap sees the adjacent roadmaps where their knowledge touches — and the members who are deep in those adjacent roadmaps.

Community events: structured sessions where members at different depths in connected roadmaps present what they know and ask what they cannot reach. Not lectures — genuine exchanges, where the person with the narrow expertise and the person with the broad context each find their understanding reorganized by the encounter.

The long-term community aspiration: a network of interconnected mastery deep enough and wide enough that any question about any subject can be routed to the person whose learning has brought them closest to the answer — and whose answer will point to the next person whose learning brings them closer still.

vision: The master historian can speculate on how a single moment butterflies entire empires — with precision, with humility, and with respect for the evidence. MasterMaker builds the community where those speculations are earned, tested, refined, and honored.

title: The Food Forge — Leone University's Culinary Creation Club
summary: A community-powered food innovation platform where members post original recipes, earn coins for community-validated creations, and can sell licensed food products directly through the platform — all feeding into a CookBot that aggregates culinary data and provides AI-driven cooking guidance.

sections.heading: The Forge Model
sections.content:
The Food Forge is the origination point for food ideas. Members post original recipes — documented with ingredients, technique, photos, and tasting notes. The community rates and discusses them. High-rated creations earn Forge Coins, the platform's internal currency, redeemable for purchases from other members' food products.

This creates a circular economy: creative contribution is rewarded, and the reward funds access to more creativity from others.

sections.heading: The Marketplace Layer
sections.content:
Members who are licensed to sell food products can list their creations in the Forge Marketplace. Forge Coins and standard currency are both accepted. The platform handles discovery and payment; the producer handles production and fulfillment.

From there, the marketplace integrates with external platforms — helping producers list their products beyond the Forge and build independent food businesses from a community foundation.

sections.heading: The CookBot Intelligence Layer
sections.content:
Every recipe submitted, rated, and purchased feeds into CookBot — an AI system that aggregates culinary data at scale: flavor combinations that work, techniques that improve specific outcomes, ingredient substitutions that maintain result quality.

CookBot provides personalized cooking guidance: given your preferences, your pantry, and your skill level, it generates novel recipe suggestions and helps you understand why your last attempt produced the result it did.

vision: Food is the most universal human creative act. The Food Forge makes it collaborative, rewarding, and endlessly generative.
